headline: PHP2Shell flaws now successfully exploited in the wild; AI coding agent lure, LiteLLM 1.107.0 and Tailscale SSH flaws stay open

bullets.text: New: BleepingComputer reports PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) is now being successfully exploited in the wild, beyond earlier attempts and suspected North Korean scanning. Fixes are in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; a third bug, CVE-2026-115560, will not get an emergency fix.

The Hacker News reports a malicious file left in a Downloads folder that tries to trick an AI coding agent into installing malware. Agents that read local files can be steered by content planted in them.

CISA's deadline is today (Oct 26) for exploited SQL injection in Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-114625), its third zero-day in four months, and OS command injection in Collabora Online's CODE server (CVE-2026-110447).
LiteLLM: a leaked master key let attackers steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. Version 1.107.0 on PyPI and Docker stole credentials through Python startup hooks.
Still unpatched: Tailscale SSH flaws could let a hacked device on a tailnet reach root on other servers. No fix is named yet.
Breaches: Quest Diagnostics patient personal and health data (3 outlets), 11.7 million CAPCOM ID accounts, and over 70,000 firewall and VPN credentials exposed.

actions: Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 today, rebuild images that bundle PHP, restart PHP-FPM or Apache, and check exposed PHP hosts for compromise.
Run AI coding agents with approval required for installs and shell commands, and don't point them at untrusted folders like Downloads.
Patch or take offline Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator and Collabora Online (CODE server) now, and check both for compromise.
Search lockfiles, images and CI caches for litellm 1.107.0. If it ever ran, treat the host as compromised and rotate every credential it could read.
If you use Tailscale SSH, tighten ACLs so only trusted devices can SSH to servers, and watch for Tailscale's fix.
Patch self-managed GitLab and update Ruby and Pillow.
